problem: Visuomotor policies tied to a specific robot's action and observation spaces are difficult to transfer across different kinematic structures.
contribution: LEGATO uses a shared handheld grasping tool/interface, motion-invariant trajectory regularization and constrained low-level motion retargeting.
algorithm: Train a high-level recurrent visual policy from tool demonstrations with trajectory likelihood, DHB motion-invariant loss and gripper classification. Retarget desired tool motion through prioritized Jacobian constraints and eSNS/QP-style velocity-level limits.
observations: Egocentric stereo camera features and recent policy actions expressed through the common grasping-tool interface.
actions: Desired handheld-tool trajectories inSE3 and discrete grasping actions at10Hz, subsequently mapped to embodiment-specific joint/whole-body motion.
embodiment_and_data: Simulation Abstract, Panda, Spot, GR1 and GoogleRobot embodiments, plus real deployments using the common tool; lid closing, cup shelving and ladle reorganization.
experiments: Compare representation regularization, demonstration embodiment and deployment morphology with consistent initial robot states and randomized object poses. Simulation success is evaluated on50trials per reported setting.
baselines: BC-RNN, DiffusionPolicy and LEGATO with onlySE3 trajectory supervision, isolating the invariant regularizer from the common interface.

quantitative_result.reason: The50trial comparison and aggregate margins were examined, but individual plot bar values were not digitized.

limitations: A physically shared gripper/tool reduces both contact and observation differences; Explorer's different grippers do not automatically satisfy this assumption. Fixed-base workspace and tracking/IK errors reduce transfer, especially on large-motion tasks.
hardware_adaptation: Use constrained FK/IK as a known baseline and evaluate an object/tool-relative effect representation separately. Admit only poses achievable by the actual ROSMASTER joint count and limits; do not force arbitrary6DoF targets onto an underactuated arm.
algorithm_detail: DHB invariants regularize predicted gripper motion rather than directly generate it. Low-level priorities track tool pose then posture bias, while inequality constraints cover joint position/velocity/acceleration and Cartesian/collision limits. The policy and constrained realization are distinct components.
integration_contract: Bind tool/camera transforms, metricSE3 conventions, grasp semantics, target kinematic chain, reachability and velocity/acceleration bounds. Record retargeting residuals and rejected targets rather than silently clipping them.
license_evidence: Primary RA-L/arXiv full text read; no official code/license verified, so an attributed independent FK/IK baseline must not be described as reused LEGATO implementation.
required_experiments: FK/IK round-trip and unreachable-pose tests; shared-gripper versus different-gripper scope analysis; same-scene target-only comparison; SE3 versus invariant/effect ablation with equal data; independent physical outcome after supervised approval.
difference_from_explorer: Common task-space interfaces and retargeting are prior work. The proposed evidence-grounded reuse mechanism needs gains beyond a numerical IK mapping.
